newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end strong on month-end buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end strong on month-end buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose sharply in tandem with Wall Street Thursday as traders prepared to square their accounts at the end of the month.
"There was selective month-end buying, foreign investors stepped in and stocks leaving the overbought zone led the way," said Hector Jimenez, a technical analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index rose 41.30 points, or 1.1 percent, to 3,672.92.
"Today's gains were important because they underscored the short-term upward channel in which the bourse is trading. We were close to support at the close yesterday," Jimenez said.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 83.12 points, or 1.2 percent, to 6,823.86.
Some traders said gains on Mexican shares listed in New York also bolstered the Mexican market.
Market heavyweight Telmex's ADRs ended up 7/8 at 37-7/8, while its L shares advanced 38 centavos (five cents) to 14.90 pesos ($1.90).
Transportation company TMM's ADRs gained 7/8 to 6-3/4, while its A shares headed the gainers' list after closing up 5.70 pesos ($0.73) at 42.00 pesos ($5.36).

"Dealers were buying (TMM) all day, obviously because of the payment they will make for the railroad concession they won. The stock was hit hard long after they tendered their bid and it might even rally further," a trader said.
TMM announced this week it will pay $280 million as part of its stake in the recently awarded concession to run Mexico's Northeast Railway.
On the broad market, gainers beat losers 68 to 27.
Bancrecer financial group headed the decliners, down 10 centavos (one cent) to 1.22 pesos (16 cents). Traders noted financial stocks got hurt after disappointing earnings from Banacci last week.
Another big loser was Tekchem, down 10 centavos (one cent) to 2.28 pesos (29 cents).
